title: Active learning identifies high-performing electrolyte solvents for anode-free lithium metal cells
summary: Researchers used sequential Bayesian experimental design with Bayesian model averaging to select electrolyte solvents for testing in Cu||LiFePO4 cells, feeding cycle-capacity results back into the model over seven campaigns. The study reports seven top-performing solvent electrolytes and says four distinct solvents rival state-of-the-art performance; three were previously unreported as electrolytes for anode-free cells. Five of nine compounds tested in the final batch exceeded 100 mAh/g discharge capacity at cycle 20. The result is limited to the tested cell configuration and cycling conditions and does not establish commercial battery performance.
ai_technology: Active learning with sequential Bayesian experimental design, Bayesian model averaging and Gaussian-process surrogate models

evidence.tested: Electrolytes were tested iteratively in Cu||LiFePO4 cells. The study reports seven top-performing solvents; three had not previously been reported as anode-free battery electrolytes, and four distinct solvents rivaled state-of-the-art performance. Five of nine batch-7 electrolytes exceeded 100 mAh/g discharge capacity at cycle 20.
evidence.unknown: Performance is limited to the reported cell chemistry, 1 M LiFSA configuration and cycling protocol; it does not establish full-cell energy density, lifetime in commercial formats or manufacturing readiness.
evidence.ai_role: A sequential active-learning framework selected each batch of candidate solvents using Bayesian experimental design and Bayesian model averaging, then incorporated measured electrochemical outcomes to update its next selections.
